images.title: Two right angles, no triangle
images.purpose: Show that two base angles of 90° give arms that stay side by side and never meet.
images.composition: One horizontal base low in the frame with two tall parallel arms rising from its ends; wide white space above and around.
exact_structure: A dark horizontal segment AB near the bottom centre, A at the left end and B at the right end.
A teal (#0072B2) arm rising straight up from A, and an amber (#E69F00) arm rising straight up from B, both the same length and drawn as plain arrows that run off toward the top without meeting.
A small reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right-angle mark at A and another at B, each labelled 90°.
A thin dashed grey (#6B7280) double-headed gap marker halfway up between the arms, to show the distance stays the same.
Nothing else: no third side, no triangle drawn.
rejection: the arms drawn leaning toward each other or meeting at a point
an angle other than 90° at A or B
images.takeaway: If both base angles are 90° or more, the arms never meet, so there is no triangle.
images.description: A base AB with two parallel arms rising at 90° from its ends and never meeting.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Let students predict, then point at the constant gap between the two arms.

image_decisions.why: The picture shows the core reason no triangle forms when two angles are 90° or more.
